title: Customer Service Administrator
description:
Customer Service Administrator

Customer Service Administrator Hours & Pay:

title: Family Legal Secretary
description:
Legal Secretary
A leading Kent-based law firm are seeking a Legal Secretary to join their busy Family Team based in Maidstone. This firm are recognised in the Legal 500 and have an excellent reputation across Kent, Sussex and further afield. The successful Family Legal Secretary will be welcomed by a friendly and warm environment, modern offices and lots of fun social events throughout the year.
The successful Family Legal Secretary will be supporting a small team of Solicitors and Legal Executives and will be an important, pivotal part of this exciting group of legal professionals.
This is a busy and fast-paced role that requires good time management, strong administrative skills and great client care skills. It is essential that you have experience of working as a Legal Secretary/Administrator within a Family department, with a good understanding of the demands of this type of role.
The duties of this role include, but are not limited to:
- Support with the administrative aspects of family law - opening and closing files, on boarding clients, diary management, preparing file bundles etc
- Prepare and draft legal documents related to family law
- Liaise with clients, solicitors and other relevant parties to obtain necessary information or documentation.
- Attending client meetings - note taking where appropriate.
- Respond to telephone and email inquiries in a professional manner.
- Maintain and update files and databases.
- Organise and schedule appointments and meetings, as necessary.
- Track key deadlines, ensuring all required actions are promptly undertaken.
- Preparing invoices, tracking payments, and managing financial records.

Requirements:
- Proven experience as a Family Legal Secretary or similar role within Family law.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Proficient in MS Office and legal software.
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
- Exceptional time management skills.
- Knowledge of the conveyancing process.
- Excellent interpersonal skills.
- Ability to work independently as well as part of a team, effectively collaborating with colleagues.

Benefits:
- Opportunity for hybrid working (after 6 months service)
- 23 days holiday + bank holidays + Christmas eve + Birthday
- Pension scheme
- Death in Service (3x Salary)
- Private Medical Insurance (after 12 months service)
- 15% off legal services
- Employee Assistance Programme

Job type: Full-time, permanent

Salary: 27,000 - 35,000 (depending on experience)

title: Clinical Administrator
description: This is a key role within our multidisciplinary team, supporting clinicians by ensuring incoming clinical correspondence is reviewed, processed and accurately recorded. You will identify relevant clinical information, update patient records and ensure correspondence is directed to the right person or team. The role will suit someone who enjoys working with detailed information, follows processes carefully and can use their judgement to identify what can be safely managed and what needs clinical input. You will help reduce unnecessary GP workload while recognising when something is outside your remit and needs to be escalated. Day-to-day work may include reviewing hospital letters, investigation results and other clinical correspondence, extracting and coding relevant information, updating patient records, filing documentation and directing tasks to the appropriate team. You may also support note summarising and other activities that maintain clear, accurate clinical records. Accuracy and patient safety are at the heart of this role. You will need to manage your workload, follow practice and national guidance, and know when to seek advice from a GP, supervisor or manager. By ensuring clinical information is handled accurately, promptly and safely, you will help our clinicians work effectively and support patient care. As a Clinical Administrator, you will help keep the practices clinical and administrative processes running smoothly. Your main duties will include processing incoming clinical correspondence, accurately updating patient records, reviewing and coding clinical information, and ensuring information is directed to the appropriate team member. You will support the processing of hospital and clinic letters, results, safeguarding information and electronic data, as well as summarising new patient records, supporting registrations and managing out-of-area correspondence. Working closely with the clinical team, you will identify and escalate complex or sensitive issues appropriately and support effective communication across the practice. You will also contribute to team meetings and training and help new colleagues learn practice processes. High standards of confidentiality, information governance and accuracy are essential. Job Description Clinical Administrator Job Title: Clinical Administrator Responsible to: Administration Lead, Practice Manager Accountable to: Practice Partnership Hours: Applicants must be available to work within our core operating hours of 08:00-17:30 . We are open to discussing flexibility around shift length and working patterns for the right candidate. Job Summary The Clinical Administrator provides vital support to the multidisciplinary team by managing and processing clinical correspondence and patient records in line with practice and national guidelines. The role focuses on streamlining workflows to reduce unnecessary GP administration, ensuring accurate coding and filing of information, and directing more complex items to the appropriate clinician for review. The post-holder will work as part of the Clinical Administration team, prioritising their workload effectively, maintaining strict confidentiality at all times, and knowing when to escalate matters to supervisors or clinicians. Roles and Responsibilities Ensure all incoming and internal correspondence is stored in patient records. Review and Read Code clinical correspondence before forwarding to clinicians. Process and file hospital letters, reports, emails and other correspondence. Code diagnoses, procedures and investigations accurately. Refer complex or high-risk documents, including safeguarding issues, to the relevant clinician. Summarise new patient records (manual and GP2GP) and process registrations, transfers, and out-of-area notifications. Manage incoming test results, redirect unmatched pathology, and process screening and monitoring results. Process Out of Hours reports and other external communications. Monitor the practice email inbox, flagging urgent queries promptly. Provide administrative cover for other team members when necessary. Open, scan, distribute and file post; manage photocopying and record requests. Assist with training and mentoring of new staff. Maintain a tidy office environment and adhere to a clear desk policy. Teamwork & Communication Work as part of the Clinical Administration Team and the wider practice team. Build effective working relationships with colleagues, patients and external organisations. Communicate clearly and professionally, ensuring confidentiality at all times. Participate in meetings and training, including occasional sessions outside normal hours. General Responsibilities Confidentiality Patients entrust the practice with sensitive information and staff must respect this confidentiality at all times. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues or the practice may only be shared in line with GDPR and practice policies. Health & Safety Follow practice health and safety policies, including infection prevention and control. Use personal security systems as required. Identify risks, manage work safely, and report concerns promptly. Maintain work areas in a safe, hazard-free condition. Equality & Diversity Promote equality of opportunity and respect the rights of patients, carers and colleagues. Act in ways that recognise diversity and ensure fairness, consistent with policy and legislation. Respect privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs at all times. Personal & Professional Development Participate in annual appraisal and performance reviews. Take responsibility for ongoing learning and development. Share skills and knowledge with colleagues and support new staff training. Quality Strive to maintain quality and safety within the practice. Reflect on individual and team activities, suggesting improvements to enhance performance. Manage own time, workload and resources effectively. Communication Communicate effectively with patients, carers, colleagues and external agencies. Adapt communication methods to meet individual needs and ensure understanding. Other Information Duties may change according to practice needs, following consultation and training. The role is subject to the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act (1974) exceptions, requiring disclosure of relevant convictions. The practice operates a non-smoking policy.

title: Receptionist
description: We are looking for a friendly, reliable and motivated Receptionist to join our welcoming team at Len Valley Practice. Our reception team plays a vital role in the day-to-day running of the practice, providing the first point of contact for our patients and helping to ensure they receive a positive and supportive experience. This is a varied and busy role, offering plenty of opportunity to develop your skills and become an important part of the team. You will need to be confident communicating with people face to face and over the telephone, have good organisational and administrative skills, and be comfortable managing a range of tasks in a fast-paced environment. Being approachable, patient and able to use your own initiative are all important qualities. The practice is open from 08:00 to 18:30 , and the successful candidate must be available to work across these hours. Shifts will vary, with flexibility around the individual shift pattern, but the start and finish times will remain within these set opening hours. Some additional flexibility may also be required to provide cover during periods of staff absence or annual leave. If you enjoy working with people, like no two days being quite the same and want to be part of a friendly team making a real difference to patients, we would love to hear from you The Receptionist will act as the first point of contact for patients and visitors, ensuring all enquiries are dealt with courteously, efficiently and confidentially. Core responsibilities include welcoming visitors, managing incoming calls, taking accurate messages and appointment requests, and processing patient registrations and online access applications. The post-holder will support the smooth running of the practice by managing administrative tasks such as scanning and filing documents, handling correspondence, sending recall letters, updating noticeboards and ensuring the reception and waiting areas remain clean, tidy and well-stocked. Additional duties include relaying verified test results, advising patients on fees for non-NHS services, assisting with patient complaints at first contact, and handing over outstanding matters to colleagues at the end of each shift. The Receptionist will also contribute to patient safety by following established procedures, maintaining confidentiality, and escalating queries when appropriate. As part of the wider reception team, the post-holder will attend meetings, support colleagues, assist with mentoring new staff, and uphold the high standards of professionalism, communication and service expected by the practice. Job Title: Receptionist Responsible to: Practice Manager Accountable to: Practice Partnership Job Summary The practice is seeking someone who is an excellent communicator, reliable and able to work on their own initiative. A degree of flexibility is also highly sought after to enable the successful post-holder to provide extra hours to cover for sickness and holiday periods. The receptionist role represents a great opportunity for those with great administrative skills, who enjoy working within the busy environment of a GP practice. Patient Reception and Communication Welcome patients and visitors to the practice, ensuring all enquiries are handled in a friendly, approachable, courteous and confidential manner. Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and professionally, dealing with enquiries where possible or directing calls to the appropriate member of the team. Take accurate telephone messages, appointment details and home visit requests, ensuring all relevant information is recorded on the computer system and passed to the appropriate person. Manage incoming patient tasks and requests, checking inboxes, workflows and emails regularly and ensuring these are dealt with or directed appropriately. Relay test results to patients once they have been reviewed and verified by a GP. Remind doctors of outstanding telephone calls, home visits or other requests as appropriate. Handle initial verbal complaints or concerns sensitively and professionally, seeking advice from the Lead Receptionist or referring to the Practice Manager where necessary. Assist patients with new patient registrations and registration for Online Patient Access, explaining the relevant procedures. Advise patients of applicable charges for certificates, claim forms, medical examinations and other services. General Administrative Duties Ensure scanning of documents and incoming mail is completed accurately and promptly. Ensure external and internal mail is passed to the appropriate administration team for processing. Assist with sending patient recall letters and other correspondence, using email where appropriate. File patient medical records and documentation appropriately. Ensure outstanding matters and relevant information are handed over to colleagues at the end of each shift. Ensure start-of-day and end-of-day checklists are completed. Reception and Practice Environment Ensure the reception area and waiting room are clean, tidy and welcoming. Maintain adequate supplies of stationery and forms at reception, requesting further copies to be printed at Harrietsham when required. Keep noticeboards up to date and ensure appropriate patient information and literature is displayed. Ensure all visitors are asked to sign in and out of the visitors' book. Ensure deliveries signed for by reception are passed to the appropriate person. Contribute to maintaining a safe and secure working environment. Teamwork and Professional Responsibilities Be fully conversant with reception procedures, protocols and any practice developments. Assist with the induction, mentoring and training of new reception team members where required. Attend and participate in reception, staff and other meetings as required. Maintain a smart and professional appearance and communicate politely and respectfully at all times. Maintain strict confidentiality and adhere to practice policies and procedures. Undertake any other reasonable duties as required to support the smooth running of the practice. Appraisal and Training Participate in the practice appraisal process and complete any agreed learning and development objectives. Attend training courses and development sessions as considered necessary by the Practice Manager. The Successful Post-Holder Will Need to Demonstrate Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate confidently and sensitively with patients and colleagues. A friendly, approachable and patient-focused manner, with a commitment to providing a high standard of service. Good organisational and administrative skills, with strong attention to detail. The ability to remain calm, professional and efficient in a busy and sometimes challenging environment. The ability to work independently, use initiative and recognise when matters need to be escalated. Good IT skills and confidence using computer systems. A flexible and supportive approach to working as part of a team. The ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information appropriately.
